1.en: Say ‘I seek refuge in the Lord of the Daybreak the morning

2.en: from the evil of what He has created of obligated animate beings and non-obligated ones and from all inanimates such as poison and so on;
2.ar: ﴿مِن شَرّ ما خَلَقَ﴾ مِن حَيَوان مُكَلَّف وغَيْر مُكَلَّف وجَماد كالسُّمِّ وغَيْر ذَلِكَ

3.en: and from the evil of darkness when it gathers that is from night when it becomes dark and the moon when it is absent
3.ar: ﴿ومِن شَرّ غاسِق إذا وقَبَ﴾ أيْ اللَّيْل إذا أظْلَمَ والقَمَر إذا غابَ

4.en: and from the evil of the women-blowers sorceresses who blow on knots which they knot into strings blowing into them certain words but without spittle; however al-Zamakhsharī says ‘with this spittle’ — sorceresses such as the daughters of the said Labīd —
4.ar: ﴿ومِن شَرّ النَّفّاثات﴾ السَّواحِر تَنْفُث ﴿فِي العُقَد﴾ الَّتِي تَعْقِدها فِي الخَيْط تَنْفُخ فِيها بِشَيْءٍ تَقُولهُ مِن غَيْر رِيق، وقالَ الزَّمَخْشَرِيّ مَعَهُ كَبَناتِ لَبِيد المَذْكُور

5.en: and from the evil of an envier when he envies’ when he manifests his envy and behaves in accordance with it — such as the mentioned Labīd from among the Jews who were envious of the Prophet s; the mention of these three elements of evil which are already subsumed by the statement ‘of what He has created’ is because of the severity of their evil.
5.ar: ﴿ومِن شَرّ حاسِد إذا حَسَدَ﴾ أظْهَر حَسَدَهُ وعَمِلَ بِمُقْتَضاهُ، كَلَبِيد المَذْكُور مِن اليَهُود الحاسِدِينَ لِلنَّبِيِّ ﷺ، وذِكْر الثَّلاثَة الشّامِل لَها ما خَلَقَ بَعْده لِشِدَّةِ شَرّها.
